[task] Determinism contract as tests: byte-identical rebuilds + flavor-swap diff confined to style layer
description:
Two invariants from the vision (CONTEXT.md 'Bitter-lesson resistant', 'Flavor'):

1. Same binary + same inputs -> byte-identical HTML. Test: build a fixture playlist twice, assert identical output bytes. Guards against nondeterminism creeping in (hashmap iteration order, timestamps, randomized ids).
2. One-command restyle guarantee: building with --flavor a vs --flavor b may differ ONLY in the flavor style layer (<style data-flavor> block + flavor assets/font imports), never in content markup. Test: build fixture with two flavors, diff, assert changes confined. Without this test a flavor will eventually grow a content-altering hook and the guarantee dies silently.

title: Octo LayoutEditor: derive drag anchors from layout structure (no format extensions)
description:
Per docs/adr/0001-satellites-never-extend-core-formats.md, templates must NOT carry editor-specific fields (no dragPos values, no named v-drag anchors, no parallel .md template format).

The TemplateEditor instead:
- Derives draggable handles from existing template structure: {{slot}} placeholders and sldr-* classed elements are the anchors (the DOM is already enumerable).
- Writes positions back as standard CSS (grid areas, order, alignment) — the core's existing layout language. The editor manipulates what the format already expresses: slot arrangement, alignment, grid. No free pixel coordinates / absolute positioning.
- Keeps editor-only state (snap grids, selection, UI hints) in Octo's own files, never in core templates.

Templates remain the core .html format in crates/sldr-renderer/templates/. Any new template shipped for Octo demos (title-slide, code-demo, comparison, ...) is a plain core template that must make sense to a user who has never seen Octo.

title: [task] Artifact tiers per ADR-0006: directory default, --single-file opt-in with size warnings, .sldr bundle format
description:
Per docs/adr/0006-artifacts-and-the-source-artifact-boundary.md:

- Default build output: presentation directory (index.html + media siblings, relative refs) — browser-native, streams/seeks video over file://, no ceiling.
- --single-file flag: inline all media as data URIs; warn at the video memory ceiling (~tens of MB). Inversion of today's behavior where inlining is implicit.
- .sldr bundle: plain zip (renamed) containing sources — playlist, referenced slides, layouts, flavor, media — optionally cached baked HTML. 'sldr open talk.sldr' builds/presents; import folds sources into the library. Structure validated (must contain a playlist).
- Build boundary rule: artifacts never reference machine/platform paths; all source refs resolved at build.
- Warn-never-refuse on degraded self-containedness (network iframes, unbundled media) per ADR-0005.
- Docs: README/CLAUDE.md must stop headlining 'single HTML file' as default; headline is the podium test (offline, zero runtime services).

Depends on vocabulary rename (trx-x7xv) for playlist naming inside the bundle format.

title: [task] Syntect inline styles leak flavor into content markup — move to class-based highlighting
description:
Found while writing the determinism tests (crates/sldr-renderer/tests/determinism.rs): a flavor's [code] syntax_theme feeds syntect which emits inline style attributes on spans INSIDE slide content markup. Two flavors with different syntax themes therefore produce different content-region bytes — violating the confined-diff restyle guarantee (ADR-0003) and breaking runtime flavor switching for code blocks (the T toggle swaps CSS, not inline span styles).

Fix: syntect ClassedHTMLGenerator (class-based output) + per-theme CSS emitted into the flavor's <style data-flavor> block. Then code highlighting becomes part of the style layer and swaps correctly at runtime. Afterward, drop the same-theme restriction in the determinism tests.

title: [epic] Image collage layouts — 1-to-N images with multiple arrangements
description:
User request: 'i want templates for image collages for 1-n images. different layouts: skewed overlapping, tidy grid, row with subtitles under each image. circular (or other shapes) cutout in 1 or multiple rows with optional subtitles (think employee overview).'

Goal: ship a small family of slide layouts that accept a markdown list of images (with optional captions/subtitles) and arrange them in editorial-quality compositions. Same content shape, different visual treatment per layout.

Markdown convention (proposed): each image is a markdown image with optional alt-as-caption. Order in markdown determines render order. Captions come from frontmatter `captions:` array OR are pulled from the alt text. 1-N images supported.

Example slide markdown:
  ---
  layout: image-grid
  ---
  # Our team
  
  ![Anna, Engineering](anna.jpg)
  ![Bilal, Design](bilal.jpg)
  ![Chen, Research](chen.jpg)

Rendering rules:
- All collage layouts handle 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6+ images gracefully (CSS grid auto-fit + max-width)
- Captions appear below each image (optional — toggled by per-layout convention or absence of alt text)
- Hover/active states minimal — these are slides, not gallery UIs

Sub-tasks:
- .1 Tidy grid (1-N images, square or 4:3 cells, equal spacing)
- .2 Skewed/overlapping collage (rule-of-thirds asymmetric)
- .3 Row with subtitles under each image
- .4 Circular/shape-cutout employee grid (1+ rows, optional captions)

Each sub-task ships: layout name, base.css rules consuming flavor tokens, sample slide in the bundled deck, doc snippet.

title: [task] Layouts become data: user-authorable layout files (HTML structure + scoped CSS) replace hardcoded wrap_slide match arms
description:
Per docs/adr/0003-the-factoring-is-the-product.md. Today layouts are a closed set: hardcoded match arms in crates/sldr-renderer/src/template.rs (wrap_slide) with layout CSS welded into base.css. An agent or user cannot author a new layout without recompiling the binary — the bitter-lesson violation in the current design.

Target:
- A layout is a file: HTML structure with named slots ({{heading}}, {{left}}, ...) plus its scoped CSS, loaded from the configured template/layout dir; built-ins ship as the same file format embedded in the binary (include_str), user dir overrides/extends.
- Layout CSS binds ONLY to flavor tokens (var(--sldr-*)) — the contract that keeps arbitrary flavor x layout combinations and one-command restyle working.
- The slot/sldr-* class conventions are the format contract; satellites derive editor anchors from this structure (ADR-0001), so no editor-specific fields.
- Resolve the current three-way 'template' overload along the way: hardcoded layouts in template.rs, apparently-unused crates/sldr-renderer/templates/*.html, and .md scaffolds in template_dir for 'sldr new'. SlideMetadata carries both 'template' and 'layout' fields — collapse to one.
- Determinism contract unchanged: same binary + same inputs (now including layout files) -> byte-identical HTML.

title: [task] In-file language blocks in the slide format + warn-on-fallback
description:
Per docs/adr/0007-axes-are-build-parameters.md. All languages of a slide live in ONE file: shared frontmatter, layout, media refs, and step structure; only prose varies (no talk_de.md forks — translation drift).

- Decide and implement the delimiter syntax (e.g. fenced ::: lang de regions or per-step language sections) — this touches the core slide format, so settle it before/alongside trx-gckd so layouts and the source map are born language-aware.
- Build with --lang X: slide missing language X falls back to the deck default language WITH a loud warning — never silently.
- Translation is agent work, in-file; deprecation/curation unaffected (the slide stays the unit).

title: [epic] Visual flavor builder + agent-driven slide pipeline
description:
Sldr's two near-term moats: (1) a visual flavor builder that shows ALL templates with placeholder content, with live-update previews so humans and agents can dial in style; (2) an agent-driven slide pipeline where external skills (URL-to-slide, screenshot-to-slide, PPTX import, etc.) drive sldr via a stable HTTP/CLI API.

Architectural split: sldr exposes APIs and a self-describing skill; agents bring content. Sldr does NOT fetch URLs, OCR images, or summarize articles — those are external agent jobs. Sldr does: slide CRUD, asset intake, deterministic rendering, annotation loop.

Sub-issues track the foundation pieces in dependency order.

title: [task] sldr corpus dump — emit slides + flavors + templates as in-context bundle for agents
description:
Single command that emits the entire slide/flavor/template corpus as a structured bundle (markdown sections or JSON) suitable for in-context agent consumption.

CLI: 'sldr corpus' or 'sldr corpus --json' or 'sldr corpus --filter slides:tag=ai'.

Use cases:
- Agent authoring a new slide: load the corpus to see how existing slides are written.
- Agent authoring a new flavor: load existing flavors as few-shot examples.
- Agent authoring a new template: load existing templates as few-shot examples.

Why: the bitter-lesson move. Quality of agent-generated artifacts improves automatically as LLMs improve, with no engine changes — but only if we make it trivial to feed the existing corpus as in-context examples.

Pairs with future 'sldr flavor new --prompt' and 'sldr slide new --prompt' — both would call this internally to assemble few-shot context.

title: [bug] image-left/image-right ::content:: ::image:: markers not parsed
description:
render_markdown only recognized ::left::/::right:: column markers. The ::content:: and ::image:: markers used by image-left/image-right layouts passed through as raw text — slide displayed 'side by side' as broken layout with literal '::content::' and '::image::' visible.

Fix: Added MarkdownOutput::ContentImage variant in crates/sldr-renderer/src/markdown.rs. Parser handles markers in either order. wrap_slide in template.rs picks DOM order based on layout name (image-left puts image first, image-right puts content first), emits .sldr-col-content / .sldr-col-image divs that match base.css grid rules.

title: [bug] Presenter slides ghost/stuck on rapid keypress
description:
Animation cleanup relied on the 'animationend' event, which doesn't fire when an animation is interrupted by another. Rapid arrow-key navigation (faster than the 400ms transition) left previous slides at fractional opacity, still .active, still display:flex, partially overlaying the new slide.

Fix: Replaced animationend listeners with setTimeout-based cleanup (TRANSITION_MS + 50ms buffer). The timeout always fires regardless of interruption, and cleanups are idempotent so running them multiple times is safe.

Verified: 3 passes of full-deck rapid arrow-key navigation, 0 stuck-slide issues, all opacities settle to 1.

[task] sldr serve daemon — agent HTTP API (slides, skeletons, assets, build)
description:
Promote the flavor-builder HTTP server (crates/sldr-cli/src/commands/flavor_builder.rs) into a general-purpose 'sldr serve' daemon that external agents can drive without paying CLI process-launch overhead per call.

Endpoints (all JSON):
- GET /api/slides — list slides with frontmatter
- GET /api/slides/{name} — fetch one slide (markdown + parsed frontmatter)
- POST /api/slides — create a slide from JSON spec (reuse sldr slides create logic)
- PATCH /api/slides/{name} — partial update (frontmatter or body)
- DELETE /api/slides/{name}
- GET /api/skeletons, POST /api/skeletons, POST /api/skeletons/{name}/append, etc.
- POST /api/assets — accept base64'd image bytes, return a stable filename. Lets agents create slides without filesystem access.
- POST /api/build/{skeleton} — trigger a build, return path to output.
- GET /api/sample — sample-deck markdown sources + rendered HTML (the agent's catalog of available templates).
- GET /api/flavor/full — full flavor schema as JSON (every field).
- PATCH /api/flavor — partial flavor update; returns regenerated CSS.

CLI: 'sldr serve [--port N]'.

Why: agents writing slides from external content (URLs, screenshots, PPTX imports) should drive sldr over HTTP instead of forking the CLI per slide. Also enables web-to-slide tools, MCP servers, and other external skills.

Boundary: sldr handles slide/skeleton/asset CRUD + rendering. It does NOT fetch URLs, OCR, or summarize — those are agent jobs.

Depends on: trx-jbpj.1 (sample deck) for the GET /api/sample endpoint.

title: [task] sldr skill — emit self-describing agent skill file
description:
Single command that emits an evergreen skill file an agent can load wholesale into context.

CLI: 'sldr skill > SKILL.md' (or 'sldr skill --json' for structured output).

Contents:
- The full CLI command surface with worked examples.
- All JSON schemas (slide spec, skeleton spec, flavor schema).
- The HTTP API surface from 'sldr serve'.
- The sample-deck slide sources and their layouts (so the agent learns what each layout looks like by example, not by spec).
- The token vocabulary for flavors (so agents authoring flavors know what knobs exist).
- Worked examples: 'create a slide from this article', 'tweak this flavor to be more brutalist', etc.

Why: agents shouldn't need to grep the codebase to know what sldr accepts. One command, one file, always current. Updates automatically as schemas evolve because it pulls from the same Rust types via schemars.

title: [task] Source-mapped HTML output (data-src-file, data-src-range)
description:
Renderer emits data-src-file and data-src-range attributes on every block-level element in the generated HTML, mapping each rendered region back to a byte range in its source markdown file. What: - Track byte offsets through the pulldown-cmark event stream in crates/sldr-renderer/src/markdown.rs. - Emit data-src-file="slides/foo.md" and data-src-range="123-145" on

,

,

  • , 
    , 
    , 
    , etc.
- Costs a few KB per built HTML; near-zero perf hit.

Why this is foundational, not a feature:
- Enables Phase A of bidirectional editing (contenteditable changes apply back to the markdown source via watch endpoint).
- Enables annotation / comment anchoring: a tool can say 'the headline on slide 3 needs work' and resolve that to a markdown line range.
- Enables agent visual-feedback loops: an agent looking at a screenshot can ask 'which markdown produced this element' and act on the answer.

Should ship now — costs almost nothing and unblocks several downstream features.

title: [task] Annotation loop — comment intake + sldr apply-comments
description:
Human-in-the-loop iteration on agent-generated slides. Adapted from open-slide's click-to-comment → /apply-comments pattern, but kept inside sldr's deterministic-render world.

Mechanism:
- In presenter.js, add 'C' keybinding for comment mode. Click any element → inline textarea.
- Comments persist as <!-- @sldr-comment id=abc anchor=src-range body="..." --> markers inserted into the source markdown right next to the relevant block (anchor uses source-mapping from trx-jbpj.4).
- Or: comments persist in .sldr/comments/<id>.toml and reference source ranges. (Pick one; in-source markers are easier to grep, separate files are easier to diff.)
- 'sldr comments list' lists open comments.
- 'sldr apply-comments' invokes the configured agent (config.agent: opencode/claude code/codex) with: relevant slide source + flavor + comments + a worked-example prompt. Agent proposes diff. User reviews. On approval, comments are stripped and edits applied.
- HTTP equivalent: POST /api/comments accepts {slide, anchor, body}.

Why: closes the loop. An agent generates a slide from an article; the human says 'make this less corporate'; the agent edits; rinse. Today this is a manual markdown edit.

Depends on: trx-jbpj.4 (source-mapping).

title: [bug] Non-interactive resolution: TTY-detect in resolve_with_interactive, fail loud on missing/ambiguous slides
description:
Per the one-door principle (humans and agents share the same CLI), every command must be fully operable non-interactively. Today in crates/sldr-cli/src/commands/build.rs resolve_with_interactive:

1. ResolveResult::Multiple unconditionally opens a dialoguer Select prompt with no TTY check — an agent or script hangs or errors on an invisible prompt.
2. ResolveResult::NotFound prints a colored warning, returns Ok(None), and the build continues without the slide — exit code 0 for a build silently missing slides.

Fix:
- When stdin/stdout is not a TTY: ambiguity fails with nonzero exit and candidate list on stderr (machine-parseable); never prompt.
- A missing slide reference fails the build (nonzero exit) in both TTY and non-TTY modes — silent skipping misleads humans too. Consider --skip-missing to opt back in.
- Add --no-input to force non-interactive behavior even on a TTY.
Same treatment for the other resolve_with_interactive call sites (export.rs, watch.rs) and rm's interactive selection.
